annotations.title: CompactSimpleGaugeGroup Typeclass
annotations.content: The formalization introduces a custom typeclass CompactSimpleGaugeGroup capturing the essential properties: G is a compact Lie group with simple (non-abelian) Lie algebra. This allows all 273+ theorems to be polymorphic over the gauge group, applying equally to SU(2), SU(3), or any compact simple group.

annotations.title: Minkowski Metric Formalization
annotations.content: The Minkowski metric η_μν with signature (-,+,+,+) is formalized with proved properties: diagonality, symmetry, η₀₀ = -1, ηᵢᵢ = 1 for i ≥ 1, trace η^μ_μ = 2, and Lorentzian signature (1,3). The squared norm s² = -t² + x² + y² + z² is derived from diagonality.

annotations.title: The Classical Yang-Mills Equations
annotations.content: D_μ F^μν = 0 (Yang-Mills equation) and D_[μ F_νρ] = 0 (Bianchi identity). Unlike Maxwell's equations, these are non-linear because the covariant derivative D involves the gauge field A itself. This non-linearity is the source of both the richness and the difficulty of non-abelian gauge theory.

annotations.title: Gauge Transformations Form a Group
annotations.content: Gauge transformations g(x): R⁴ → G form an infinite-dimensional group under pointwise multiplication, with the Yang-Mills action invariant: S[A^g] = S[A]. This gauge symmetry is the defining feature of Yang-Mills theory and the reason gauge fixing (Faddeev-Popov, Part XXXVII) is needed for quantization.

annotations.title: Wightman QFT Axioms as Lean Structure
annotations.content: The Wightman axioms are encoded as a Lean structure with fields: Hilbert space H, vacuum state Ω, Hamiltonian H, field operators, Poincaré covariance, spectral condition (E ≥ 0), and locality (spacelike commutativity). QuantumYangMills extends this with gauge field operators, capturing the mathematical framework for rigorous QFT.

annotations.title: The Mass Gap: Spectrum Has a Gap
annotations.content: A QFT has mass gap Δ > 0 if all states orthogonal to the vacuum have energy ≥ Δ. Equivalently, the Hamiltonian spectrum is {0} ∪ [Δ, ∞). Key proved properties: any Δ' < Δ is also a mass gap (monotonicity), and vacuum energy is zero by axiom. The mass gap explains why nuclear forces are short-range.

annotations.title: Area Law vs Perimeter Law: Confinement Criterion
annotations.content: Wilson's confinement criterion: W(C) ~ exp(-σ·Area) indicates confinement (quarks bound), while W(C) ~ exp(-κ·Perimeter) indicates deconfinement (free quarks). A key proved theorem shows these are mutually exclusive: a theory cannot exhibit both behaviors simultaneously, as area grows faster than perimeter for large loops.

annotations.title: 2D Yang-Mills: The Exactly Solvable Case
annotations.content: In 2D, Yang-Mills is exactly solvable via Migdal's formula: Wilson loop expectations reduce to finite-dimensional group integrals weighted by heat kernel. The partition function Z = Σ_R (dim R)² exp(-C₂(R)·A/(2β)) sums over representations. This provides the only dimension where the mass gap can be computed explicitly.

annotations.title: Center Symmetry Z_N Classifies Confinement
annotations.content: The center Z_N of SU(N) acts on Polyakov loops P by multiplication: P → ω·P. In the confined phase (Z_N unbroken), ⟨P⟩ = 0 (averaging over center elements). In the deconfined phase, Z_N is spontaneously broken: ⟨P⟩ ≠ 0. For SU(2), Z_2 = {1,-1} with the key theorem: ω²=1 and |ω|=1 implies ω ∈ {1,-1}.

annotations.title: Gribov Copies: Global Gauge Fixing Is Impossible
annotations.content: Singer's theorem (axiomatized): for non-abelian gauge theories, no global gauge-fixing condition can uniquely select one representative from each gauge orbit. The Gribov region Ω (where the Faddeev-Popov operator is positive) has a boundary ∂Ω where det(FP) = 0, creating copies. This is a fundamental obstruction to perturbative quantization.

annotations.title: AdS/CFT and Holographic Mass Gap
annotations.content: Maldacena's AdS/CFT correspondence maps N=4 SU(N) Yang-Mills to string theory on AdS₅×S⁵. While N=4 SYM is conformal (no mass gap), deformations that break conformal symmetry can produce a mass gap. The holographic approach provides non-perturbative insights but applies to supersymmetric theories rather than pure Yang-Mills.

annotations.title: Constructive QFT: Rigorous 2D Yang-Mills
annotations.content: Constructive QFT provides mathematically rigorous definitions of quantum field theories. In 2D, Yang-Mills has been rigorously constructed (unlike 4D). The formalization covers the lattice-to-continuum limit, gauge-invariant observables, and the connection to Migdal's exact solution. This represents the state of the art for rigorous QFT.
